gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-thai: Noto Sans Thai fills its lowercase like inflated glass beads, with rounded letters left open beneath the heading above. Stencilia's structural, striking punch is the real strength of this pairing.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Thick chalk, pressed hard: Noto Sans Wancho has a hulking lowercase and an e with a wide terminal gap. And Stencilia delivers the structural, striking statement while the body font simply carries the text.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-zanaba: Noto Sans Zanabazar Square soars with a tall x-height and crisp gaps. Stencilia adds structural, striking display strength, and the two stay clearly distinct, one loud and one quietly approachable.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-traditional: Spacious gaps at its curve terminals set Stencilia apart, while Noto Traditional Nushu uses a broad-nibbed pen stroke that never curls shut. Its bowls then fill the line beneath the heading.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-prompt: Stencilia brings structural, striking letters with a compact gap between x-height and ascender line, above Prompt's oversized-looking small letters. The heading gives structure, and Prompt keeps its apertures open.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-pt-sans-caption: Unclosed bowls, big lowercase: PT Sans Caption feels inviting. Beneath Stencilia's striking display lines, a sans-serif paragraph would read in an open, contemporary, easygoing way across many lines of text.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-khula: Stentiga stretches out with opened-up tracking and refined polish. It is best at refined, luxurious display lettering, while Khula is best at holding its curves open in modern text.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-krub: Refined and luxurious, Stentiga stands wide with round bowls whose walls never swell or taper. Krub's pronounced x-height and pen-lifted loops give this pairing its sharpest contrast against the display.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Level, quiet, wide-mouthed lettering: that is Stentiga. If the heading is made small, its spread-out tracking loses force, while Noto Sans Limbu, a plain sans, stays tall-bodied and approachable.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-mayan-n: Stentiga looks refined, spaced wide, and luxurious. Noto Sans Mayan Numerals, a professional, contemporary sans-serif with tall-bodied small letters and a gaping c, would read crisp over long text.
